# Sort Integers by The Number of 1 Bits.

@example 0 has no 1 bits, 16 has one, 3, 5 and 10 have two each, and 7 has three.
[10,3,7,0,16,5]
=> [0,16,3,5,10,7]

@example 32 is the only value with a single 1 bit, so it leads; 24, 5, 9 and 6 have two each and follow from smallest to largest, with 5 twice.
[24,5,32,9,5,6]
=> [32,5,5,6,9,24]

@example 1 has one 1 bit, 10000 (10011100010000 in binary) has five, and 8191 has thirteen.
[8191,10000,1]
=> [1,10000,8191]

# A single value, at either end of the range.
[0]
=> [0]

[10000]
=> [10000]

# One value repeated.
[5,5,5,5]
=> [5,5,5,5]

# Powers of two out of order: each has one 1 bit.
[64,2,2048,1,512]
=> [1,2,64,512,2048]

# A group of equal bit count given in decreasing order: each has two 1 bits.
[96,48,24,12,6,3]
=> [3,6,12,24,48,96]

# Scrambled within each group; sorting by bit count alone, keeping the input
# order of ties, gives [4,2,20,9,17].
[20,9,4,17,2]
=> [2,4,9,17,20]

# Every value has a different bit count, given out of order.
[255,0,8191,1,31]
=> [0,1,31,255,8191]

# Three values with twelve 1 bits, then 8191 with thirteen, the most possible.
[8190,8191,8189,6143]
=> [6143,8189,8190,8191]

# Sorting by the single key bits * K + value goes wrong here for K = 1000,
# 1024 or 8192.
[7,3072,63,10000,3,1024]
=> [1024,3,3072,7,10000,63]

# Several groups with repeats, zero among them.
[0,6,1,0,5,3,8,6]
=> [0,0,1,8,3,5,6,6]

# 8192 and 10000 have bit 13 set, which a bit count of the low 13 bits
# misses: 8192 has one 1 bit and 10000 has five, like 9000.
[8192,3,10000,2,9000]
=> [2,8192,3,9000,10000]

# 300 values with two 1 bits, more than a byte-sized bucket count holds.
[6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,6,3,8,0]
=> [0,8,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6,6]

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 1 small
[7,17,20,16,11,8,17]
=> [8,16,17,17,20,7,11]

@gen 2 small
[0,14,12,2,0]
=> [0,0,2,12,14]

@gen 3 small
[5,7,4096,8192,13,8191,12,12]
=> [4096,8192,5,12,12,7,13,8191]

@gen 4 small
[6,8192,4,4]
=> [4,4,8192,6]

@gen 5 small
[1,12,7,0,3,1]

@gen 6 small
